title: Colombia Earthquake 2026 Tracker Update — Aug 24, 2026
summary: UNGRD's Aug 23, 18:30 balance held the death toll steady at 329 while revising injured down slightly to 4,592 and narrowing missing to 234 (from 247) — reconciling a discrepancy flagged two days earlier. The affected footprint widened to 494 municipios and 159,924 families (324,157 people), with structural damage growing to 31,519 homes destroyed and 178,236 damaged. Seven new aftershocks (M2.7–3.5) struck Sipí, Andagoya and Istmina, Chocó overnight into Aug 24. President de la Espriella toured Quibdó and Buenaventura, presenting the first reconstruction model home built for displaced families, while LATAM Airlines announced it will resume flights to Pereira's Matecaña airport on Aug 26 at reduced capacity.

title: Colombia Earthquake 2026 Tracker Update — Aug 23, 2026
summary: The president's latest balance (cutoff 18:30 Aug 21) puts the toll at 329 dead, 4,600 injured and 247 missing across 16 departments and 481 municipios — reopening the previously resolved department count, which Decree 1261 had fixed at 15. Cali's formal search-and-rescue phase concluded Aug 22 with the city's toll revised to 150. Reconstruction financing accelerated: Grupo Aval, Banco GNB Sudameris and Grupo Bolívar cut mortgage rates to 8% for quake victims (Bancolombia followed for loans from Aug 25), private-sector donations surpassed COP 2 trillion (~$651M), and Asobancaria banks extended COP 1.1 trillion in credit relief. New shallow aftershocks (M2.6–3.1) were recorded near Istmina, Chocó on Aug 22–23, and the president announced a Sept. 7 visit to Chocó with business leaders to design a dedicated recovery plan.

title: Colombia Earthquake 2026 Tracker Update — Aug 21, 2026
summary: President Abelardo de la Espriella signed Decree 1261 of 2026 on Aug 19, declaring a 30-day economic, social and ecological emergency across all 15 affected departments and granting the government extraordinary powers to fund reconstruction. UNGRD's latest count puts the toll at 319 dead, 4,506 injured, 260 missing and 364 rescued alive, with more than 30,000 homes destroyed and roughly 170,000 damaged across 476 municipios — sharply higher than the prior week's figures as the damage assessment widened. The departments-affected discrepancy in the Contested section is now resolved by the decree's formal list of 15 departments.
